chief_complaint: Cough, shortness of breath, and night sweats.
history_of_present_illness: A 6-week history of increasing shortness of breath on exertion, dry cough, and drenching night sweats, along with general fatigue and a weight loss of about 10kg over the past 5 months.
exposure_and_epidemiology: He travels extensively for business, with work trips to Europe, China, Korea, Japan, Singapore, and the United States in the past 6 months; he lives with his male partner, denies recreational drug use, has never smoked tobacco, was diagnosed with HIV 6 years ago, and his CD4 count was 280/μL one month ago; he is not on ART or co-trimoxazole prophylaxis and has no other significant past medical history.
vitals: Temperature 39.2°C (102.6°F), blood pressure 120/70 mmHg, pulse 100bpm, respiratory rate 26 breaths per minute, sO2 87% on air, and 97% on 15L O2.
physical_exam: He is alert, short of breath at rest but able to complete full sentences; chest is clear on auscultation, and the rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.
labs_and_diagnostics: Arterial blood gases (on air): pH 7.44, PaO2 7.6 kPa, PaCO2 3 kPa, HCO3 19 mmol/L, Base excess -3.8, Lactate 1.6 mmol/L; FBC normal; CRP 6.7 mg/dL; Creatinine, urea, bilirubin, ALT, AP, and albumin are normal; CD4 150/µL; HIV viral load 1 500000 copies/mL (fully sensitive); chest radiograph showed bilateral perihilar infiltrates; CT-pulmonary angiogram showed extensive "ground-glass" infiltrates in both lungs, especially in the lower lobes, but no evidence of pulmonary emboli or cavitations; serum β-glucan was >500 pg/mL; bronchoscopy was macroscopically normal; Grocott staining of BAL fluid revealed Pneumocystis jirovecii cystic forms, and PCR was strongly positive for P. jirovecii DNA.
differential_diagnosis: Pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP), tuberculosis, atypical bacterial pneumonia, cryptococcosis, or histoplasmosis.
management_and_clinical_course: He was treated with high-flow oxygen and started on high-dose co-trimoxazole plus prednisolone combined with a proton-pump inhibitor; his tachycardia settled with reversal of his hypoxia; oxygen was gradually weaned, and he was discharged on oral co-trimoxazole to complete a 21-day total course; 10 days into PCP treatment, he commenced antiretroviral therapy with tenofovir, emtricitabine, and efavirenz; he developed a widespread pruritic maculopapular rash, leading to co-trimoxazole being changed to clindamycin and primaquine, and efavirenz replaced by a boosted protease inhibitor; after completing PCP treatment, he was started on dapsone and pyrimethamine for secondary prophylaxis.
